一人或數人。打伴奏型、領奏獨奏、發出轉段訊號: One or several players. Play the accompaniment pattern, lead the solo, give the signals that change section
一群敦敦鼓（dunun）先打出一個固定、可辨認的循環，一面或數面金貝鼓（djem: A group of dunun drums first lays down a fixed, recognisable cycle, and one or several djembes then stand on top of that cycle to lead, vary and signal. This is the drum ensemble of the Mande region of West Africa. It does not exist for concerts; it exists so that a group of people can dance — the time of the drum ensemble is the time of the dance steps.
三顆敦敦鼓的型必須互相咬合，分開聽會覺得殘缺，合起來才是一個完整的循環。這也是為: The patterns of the three dunun have to interlock: heard separately they sound incomplete, and only together do they make a whole cycle. That is why a dunun player cannot remember only his own part: what he remembers is the whole cycle, and he is responsible for one line of it.
不同地區的習慣也不同。馬利與幾內亞的鼓隊在鼓的數量、由誰打哪一顆、以及舞台化的程: Habits differ from region to region. Ensembles in Mali and Guinea differ in the number of drums, in who plays which one, and in how far they have been adapted to the stage; in some places one player operates all three dunun, in others three players each hold one. Whichever arrangement, the logic of the division does not change: someone keeps the cycle, someone else does the talking.
不是旁觀者。鼓隊的段落由舞者的動作決定何時該換: Not bystanders. The dancers' movements decide when the drum ensemble changes section
二十世紀後半，幾內亞與馬利的國家芭蕾舞團把這套編制搬上舞台，改成一組人在台上演奏: In the second half of the twentieth century the national ballet companies of Guinea and Mali put this line-up on stage, turning it into a performance with a group playing and dancers dancing. The stage version compresses cycles that could once go on for a long time into sections of a few minutes, and it made it common for one player to operate all three dunun at once. When this version reached Europe and America it became the doorway through which most people meet the line-up.
傳統上，這套鼓樂出現在人生儀式與農業週期裡：婚禮、命名、成年、收穫、以及各種社區: Traditionally this drumming belongs to rites of passage and the farming cycle: weddings, naming ceremonies, coming of age, harvest, and community gatherings of every kind. The drum ensemble is not invited to perform; it is part of how the rite proceeds. Once the drumming starts, the dancers come into the space and the rite has begun.
先不要聽金貝鼓。先找那條最密、最規律的鈴聲，那是掛在敦敦鼓上的鐵鈴（kenken: Do not listen to the djembe first. Find the densest, most regular bell sound, the kenken hung on the dunun; once you have it, you have the beat.
再聽桑班。它的型最有個性，通常也是整個節奏的名字所在。: Then listen to the sangban. Its pattern has the most character, and it is usually where the rhythm gets its name.
和太鼓團相比，差別在時間的擁有者。太鼓沒有「一組固定循環加一個自由領奏」的結構，: Compared with a taiko ensemble, the difference is who owns time. Taiko has no structure of a fixed cycle plus a free lead; its time is spread across the shime-daiko, the ji-uchi and visual signals. The West African ensemble is clearly divided into the dunun, which keep the cycle, and the djembe, which uses it.
和森巴打擊樂隊相比，兩者都有低音層、都有領奏與訊號，差別在誰下令。巴特利亞有一位: Compared with a samba bateria, both have a bass layer and both have a lead and signals; the difference is who gives the orders. A bateria has a director whose whole job is to give orders, using the repinique and a whistle, on a scale that can reach a hundred players; in a West African ensemble the leader is a drummer himself, the signals come off the djembe, and the group lines up by itself on the dunun cycle and the bell, with nobody standing outside conducting.
和馬拉卡圖相比，差別在誰啟動段落。馬拉卡圖由領唱者以歌聲啟動段落，人聲先給、鼓聲: Compared with maracatu, the difference is who starts a section. In maracatu the lead singer starts sections with the voice — voice first, drums after; in the West African ensemble the change of section is started by a signal from the lead drum, and the song is another layer sharing the cycle with the drums, not a layer that gives orders.
循環的中線: The middle line of the cycle
打出循環中最有辨識度的型，決定這個節奏叫什麼名字: Plays the most recognisable pattern in the cycle, which decides what the rhythm is called
打出最密、最規律的型，把拍子切細，讓其他人數得準: Plays the densest, most regular pattern, dividing the beat finely so the others can count accurately
打出最疏、最重的拍點，通常對應舞步的落地。它讓整個循環有「重量」: Plays the sparsest, heaviest beat, usually matching where the dance step lands. It gives the whole cycle its weight
找有舞者的錄影。鼓的段落長度是為舞者安排的，看舞者換動作的瞬間，就能聽出訊號在哪: Look for footage with dancers. The length of the drum sections is arranged for the dancers; watch the moment a dancer changes movement and you will hear where the signal is.
掛在鼓上的鐵鈴（kenken）: The iron bell (kenken) hung on the drum
敦敦鼓定住時間，金貝鼓使用時間: The dunun holds time; the djembe uses time
敦敦鼓才是時間的擁有者。金貝鼓的自由建立在敦敦鼓的循環上；循環一亂，領奏再花俏也: The dunun are the ones who own time. The djembe's freedom is built on the dunun cycle; once the cycle goes wrong, the most elaborate lead means nothing. Without the bass and the bell holding it up, the whole ensemble has nowhere to return to.
敦敦鼓的循環一旦開始，就幾乎不變。它會持續到樂曲結束，或直到領奏鼓發出換段的訊號: Once the dunun cycle starts it barely changes. It runs to the end of the piece, or until the lead drum signals a change of section. This constancy is not stiffness but a necessity: the dancers, the singers and the djembe players all need a reference point that does not move. The bell on the dunun divides the beat finely enough, and the sangban's pattern is distinctive enough, that however dense the djembe playing, everyone still knows where each beat falls.
敦敦鼓與金貝鼓的分工，是這個編制最重要的一件事：: The division between dunun and djembe is the most important thing about this line-up:
注意領奏鼓什麼時候停下來、什麼時候換型。那就是「訊號」與「伴奏」的分界。: Notice when the lead drum stops and when it changes pattern. That is the boundary between signal and accompaniment.
獨奏之所以有力，是因為它從循環裡長出來、再回到循環裡。只聽獨奏會錯過整個編制真正: A solo is powerful because it grows out of the cycle and returns to it. Listening only to the solo misses what the whole line-up is really doing: letting a group of people share one time.
獨奏的結構也靠循環計算。領奏者不會無限自由地打，而是在固定的循環數裡發展；時間到: The shape of a solo is counted in cycles too. The leader does not play with unlimited freedom but develops within a fixed number of cycles; when the time comes he plays the closing signal and hands the music back to the accompaniment. The dance decides that length: as long as the dancers need to show what they have, that is how long the lead gives them.
節奏本身有名字，而且名字通常來自它的用途或來源地區。同一個節奏可以有不同的金貝鼓: The rhythm itself has a name, and the name usually comes from its use or from the region it comes from. One rhythm can take different djembe accompaniment patterns, but the dunun cycle is how it is recognised: change the sangban pattern and it is a different rhythm. So this tradition's repertoire is not a list of written pieces but a set of cycles, each with its own dance steps and occasions.
聽到全團突然打同一組聲音，那是齊奏；注意它有多短。: When you hear the whole group suddenly play one set of sounds, that is a unison; notice how short it is.
西非鼓樂隊（Djembe and Dunun Ensemble）— 以金貝鼓領奏: Djembe and Dunun Ensemble — a Mande drumming line-up in which the djembe leads and the dunun drums hold a fixed cycle, existing for dance. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
西非鼓樂隊｜合奏與編制百科: Djembe and Dunun Ensemble | Ensembles and instrumentation
訊號與伴奏的差別，是聽這個編制的關鍵。: The difference between signal and accompaniment is the key to hearing this line-up.
這個編制的核心原則是「低音鼓循環、高音鼓說話」。三顆敦敦鼓各有一個固定角色，金貝: The core principle of this line-up is that the bass drums cycle and the high drum talks. Each of the three dunun has a fixed role, and the djembe is the free party — but its freedom has to stand on the coordinates the dunun give.
這種鼓樂的重點是獨奏，聽獨奏最過癮。: This drumming is all about the solo, and listening to solos is the best part of it.
還有一層是歌。這個編制很少純器樂，通常有領唱與答唱，歌詞和鼓的段落互相對應。歌者: There is one more layer: song. This line-up is rarely purely instrumental; there is usually a lead singer and an answering chorus, and the words match the drum sections. Singers and drummers follow the same call-and-response logic: the lead sings a line, the group answers, and the drum inserts itself into the gaps in the answer. Drums, song and dance share one cycle, and none of them can wander far on its own.
金貝鼓手可以隨時即興，想到什麼打什麼。: A djembe player can improvise at any moment, playing whatever comes into his head.
金貝鼓是主角，敦敦鼓只是伴奏。: The djembe is the star and the dunun are just accompaniment.
金貝鼓有三種基本聲音：低音（手掌平貼鼓面中央）、中音（手指併攏、以指腹擊在鼓面靠: The djembe has three basic sounds: bass (the palm laid flat on the centre of the head), tone (fingers together, striking with the pads near the edge), and slap (fingers spread, snapping quickly on the rim). The difference between them is not only pitch: bass and tone are clearly apart in pitch, while tone and slap are told apart mainly by the way of striking and by timbre. The leader talks with their combinations. On one drumhead the bass is like the stress in a sentence and the slap is like the punctuation.
金貝鼓的伴奏型通常是短、重複、貼著敦敦鼓的循環走；訊號型則是刻意跳出循環的樂句，: A djembe accompaniment pattern is usually short, repeated, and stuck to the dunun cycle; a signal pattern is a phrase deliberately breaking out of the cycle, fixed in length and clear in outline, which means change the moment it appears. Signals have several uses: telling the dancers to change movement, telling the dunun to change section, bringing the group into unison, or ending a solo. The lead drum usually plays the signal once, the others confirm and answer; the dunun players answer with a short variation and then return to the cycle. This process of the leader proposing and the group confirming is the call-and-response structure of West African drumming.
金貝鼓通常不只一面。大型編制會有一面領奏鼓，加上幾面打固定伴奏型的鼓；小型編制可: There is usually more than one djembe. A large line-up has one lead drum plus several playing a fixed accompaniment; a small one may have a single drum doing both accompaniment and lead. The number of drums is not the point; the point is that someone has to take the role of leader.
鐵鈴掛在其中一顆敦敦鼓上（多為敦敦巴，部分地區為桑班或肯肯尼），由另一隻手敲。鈴: The bell is hung on one of the dunun (usually the dununba, in some regions the sangban or kenkeni) and struck with the other hand. Its sound is clearer than the drumhead and harder to cover
音量平衡靠的是頻率而不是音量旋鈕。金貝鼓的低音很厚，但在多面鼓同時響時容易被其他: Volume is balanced by frequency, not by a volume knob. The djembe's bass is thick, but when several drums sound at once it is easily masked by other low frequencies and hard to pick out; the bell is thin but sharp and cuts through drums and voices. Out in an open yard or courtyard the bell is the metronome everyone shares, and the players actually line up through the bell rather than through each other's bass. This also explains why the bell hangs on a dunun: the hand that is not holding a stick is free, so one hand can keep the pattern while the other keeps the bell going, and the bell becomes the metronome for the whole group.
領奏是在固定的循環數裡進行的，而且必須用其他人聽得懂的訊號進出。真正的即興發生在: Leading happens within a fixed number of cycles, and it has to enter and leave by signals the others understand. Real improvisation happens between one signal and the next, not in unlimited freedom.
齊奏（unison）是另一個重要的段落。當領奏鼓打出特定的訊號，三顆敦敦鼓會暫時: Unison is another important section. When the lead drum plays a particular signal, the three dunun leave their cycles for a moment and play the same pattern as the djembe. For those few beats every layer disappears and only one sound is left. The unison is short, usually only a few beats, but it cuts the cycle open so that the next cycle sounds new when it starts. When the unison ends, the dunun return to the cycle and the djembe returns to accompaniment or solo.
